To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the monoclonal antibody D5G2 recognizes an intracellular form of laminin‐binding 32 kD protein (LBP‐32) that is exposed by cell damage and may be useful in targeting therapeutic agents to the site of vascular injury.
a monoclonal antibody to a 55 kDa protein exposed on damaged human endothelial cells identifies laminin‐binding‐protein 32.

a monoclonal antibody which reacts in a model of endothelial damage with unfixed damaged, but not with unfisted undamaged human endothelium, was used to identify the laminin binding protein (LBP) as a target of this antibody.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a novel monoclonal antibody (D5G2), which recognizes an epitope expressed on damaged but not intact endothelium.
the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of vascular diseases.
the development of a monoclonal antibody which reacts with a laminin‐ binding protein exposed by cell damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
D5G1 and D5G2 recognize the same protein, LBP, which is a 55 kDa laminin binding protein, and that this protein is present in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells.

the D5G2 monoclonal antibody recognizes the laminin‐binding domain of the laminin‐receptor‐related protein LBP‐32, and that the antibody binds to this protein in the context of the endothelial cell membrane.
the D5G2 antibody recognizes the laminin binding protein LBP‐32, which is expressed by endothelial cells, and is increased in expression by endothelial cells after damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a monoclonal antibody to endothelial cells damaged by balloon angioplasty identifies an intracellular laminin binding protein, and that this may be useful in targeting therapeutic agents at sites in vivo of vascular injury.

the D5G2 antibody, raised against a balloon angioplastytreated endothelial cell, recognizes the laminin‐binding receptor in endothelial cells and that this protein is exposed by balloon injury to the cell surface.
the antibody D5G2 recognizes a protein of 55 Kd which has been identified as LBP‐32, a laminin‐ and collagen‐binding protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to identify a monoclonal antibody that recognizes an endothelial protein that is exposed in damaged cells but not in undamaged cells.
we were able to identify a protein that is exposed in damaged endothelium and that we were able, using this protein, to identify an antibody that can bind to the protein.
we have identified a monoclonal antibody that binds to laminin‐binding polypeptides in damaged human vascular endothelial cells.
